title: Big Take: The Real Costs of the U.S. Iran Blockade
gist: Podcast teaser: Becca Wasser and Gerry Doyle discuss rising costs of the US six-month blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, depletion of US munitions stockpiles, and the toll on personnel and future defense readiness. Little substantive detail in the text.

insights.claim: The US has maintained a six-month blockade of the Strait of Hormuz with a rising cost.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: A prolonged Hormuz blockade is a persistent energy-market risk factor.
insights.quote: the rising tab for the U.S.'s six-month-long blockade of the Strait of Hormuz

insights.claim: The war is drawing down US munitions stockpiles and has changed the US ability to defend itself in future conflicts.
